- Overestimate prices after strong positive sentiment spikes; model tends to overshoot and fail to correct quickly.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment turns negative or neutral; model often fails to recognize downward momentum.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in responding to recent sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns from positive to negative.
- When sentiment is consistently low or negative, model overcorrects upward, leading to overestimation of recovery.
- Model tends to overfit recent upward trends, especially when sentiment is high, and underestimates volatility or mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture early mean reversion after sharp spikes — especially when sentiment drops sharply.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to average out, missing short-term reversals.
- Model underestimates downward corrections after strong upward moves — especially when sentiment is high then drops.
- Avoid extrapolating recent trends when sentiment is inconsistent — model is prone to “trend chasing” errors.
- When sentiment is negative for 3+ days, model should reduce forecasted price by 5–10% relative to recent peak.
